## Summary

Scaffold and validate a post-mortem for a defect class that recurred after a fix (recurrence >= 2).

## Usage

```bash
amber break-loop --target <repo> --issue <n> --title "<title>" --recurrence <n> | amber break-loop validate --target <repo> --file <path> [--json]
```

## Command Details

```text
Scaffold and validate a post-mortem for a defect class that recurred after a fix (recurrence >= 2).
The default action scaffolds; `validate` refuses placeholder content.

Actions:
  (none)             Scaffold docs/quality/break-loops/<date>-<slug>.md; never overwrites an existing file.
  validate           Check every section is filled: ids chosen, write-back surface + test
                     anchor + runnable verification command present.

Options:
  --issue <n>        Reference number of the recurring issue, required to scaffold (recorded only, no tracker access).
  --title "<t>"      Post-mortem title, required to scaffold; needs at least one ASCII letter or digit (becomes the filename slug).
  --recurrence <n>   How many times the class has come back, required to scaffold; must be >= 2.
  --file <path>      Post-mortem file to validate (validate action).
  --json             Emit the machine-readable envelope.

Root-cause taxonomy (pick one primary by id):
  - missing-contract — The rule existed nowhere in writing, so nothing could enforce or re-teach it.
  - cross-layer-drift — Two layers disagreed because nothing kept their shared contract in step.
  - change-propagation-failure — A change landed in one place and never reached every place that depends on it.
  - verification-gap — No test anchored the behavior, so the break reached mainline without failing anything.
  - implicit-assumption — An unstated assumption held quietly until conditions changed and it stopped holding.

Prevention-mechanism menu (pick one by id):
  - contract-and-anchor — Write the contract doc section plus a mandatory test anchor that fails whenever the rule is violated. (write-back surface: docs/specs/ + tests/)
  - parity-guard — Extend an existing coverage or parity walk so the drift itself fails CI. (write-back surface: the relevant parity test)
  - centralized-helper — Replace scattered copies with one shared helper so the class cannot re-scatter. (write-back surface: the helper module + its unit test)
  - checklist-item — Add the consideration to the ritual or wiki checklist where it will be re-read. (write-back surface: docs/wiki or the ritual doc)

Boundary: Amber scaffolds and validates — the analysis is the operator's.
No issue-tracker access, no recurrence auto-detection, no execution.

Examples:
  amber break-loop --target . --issue 122 --title "Evidence dates drift" --recurrence 2
  amber break-loop validate --target . --file docs/quality/break-loops/2026-08-15-Evidence-dates-drift.md
```
